## Documentation (Storybook)
Visit [https://textura.nintex.io/](https://textura.nintex.io/) to view the latest documentation for the Textura component library.


## Development
All of the following commands should be run from the project's root folder.

**Note:<br/>If you are creating a new component, please see "<a href="#creating-new-components">Creating new components</a>" below after getting your development environment up and running.**

### Installing dependencies

```sh
pnpm install
```

### Building the project
After installing it may be beneficial to run a preliminary build before beginning development work.
```sh
pnpm build
```

### Start the development server
This will start an instance of Storybook and should hot reload when any changes are made throughout the project.
```sh
pnpm dev
```

### Linting

```sh
# Lint all code and typescript (optionally run with fix)

pnpm lint
pnpm lint:fix
```

```sh
# Lint typescript throughout the project

pnpm lint:ts
```

### Testing
Testing in this project uses a combination of [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) and A11y testing through [Storybook's test runner](https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/accessibility-testing#automate-accessibility-tests-with-test-runner).

Testing with the [Vitest-UI](https://vitest.dev/guide/ui.html) will actively watch the code for any changes made.


```sh
# Run all tests excluding a11y (optionally with the UI and/or coverage)

pnpm test
pnpm test-ui

pnpm test:coverage
pnpm test-ui:coverage
```

```sh
# Run only a11y tests

pnpm test:a11y
```

```sh
# Run all tests including a11y

pnpm test:all
```

```sh
# Test isolated code (in this case "badge")

pnpm test badge
```

## Creating new components

Textura has built in scripting to help you get starting when creating a new component package. This will create and modify all of the necessary files required.

The resulting code generation should yield an empty, but fully working component under the new component name.

**Note:**<br/>It is recommended that this be done when there are no other active changes on the branch to allow the newly created and modified files to be seen more easily.

```sh
pnpm create:cmp

# The command will prompt you for the new component's name
? Enter component name:
```

*As components are being created and modified, please be mindful and make sure to update any relevant documentation.*

## Design Tokens

Design tokens are the single source of truth for all design-related values, such as colors, fonts, spacing, etc. They are managed in Figma and synced to the codebase to ensure consistency between design and development.

### Syncing from Figma

To sync the latest design tokens from Figma, follow these steps:

1.  **Export from Figma**: In Figma, export the design tokens as a `figma.json` file by using the [Variables Pro](https://www.figma.com/community/plugin/1264578192495051449/variables-pro-swap-import-export-variables) plugin.
2.  **Adjust the Configuration (if needed)**: Depending on the themes and tiers that need to be imported from Figma, there is a "Configuration" section on the transformation script that can be adjusted within `packages/react/scripts/transform-figma-to-tokens.ts`.
3.  **Place the File**: Place the exported `figma.json` file in the `packages/react/src/theme/tokens` directory.
4.  **Run the Script**: Run the following command from the root of the project to transform the Figma tokens into a format that can be used by the application:

```sh
pnpm build:tokens
```

### Manual Tokens

Some tokens are not managed in Figma and are instead defined directly in the codebase. These tokens can be found in the `packages/react/src/theme/tokens/non-figma-manual.ts` file. This file is intended for tokens that are specific to the application and are not part of the global design system.

### Generated Files

The `build:tokens` script will generate the following files:

*   **`packages/react/src/theme/tokens/core.ts`**: Core tokens that are shared across all themes.
*   **`packages/react/src/theme/tokens/{theme-name}/{tier}.ts`**: Theme-specific tokens, where `{theme-name}` is the name of the theme (e.g., `textura`) and `{tier}` is the tier of the token (e.g., `tier1`).
*   **`packages/react/src/theme/tokens/{theme-name}/index.ts`**: An index file that exports all the tokens for a specific theme.
